 Highlights Potential penalties in the event of withdrawal 
 Shandong Taishan precedent 
 Riyadh, Saudi Arabia – The newspaper “Okaz” has reported that Shabab Al-Ahli could face sanctions from the Asian Football Confederation’s (AFC) Disciplinary and Ethics Committee, should the club fail to travel to Saudi Arabia to play its upcoming match against Al-Hilal in the AFC Champions League Elite.
 All eyes are on the match scheduled for Tuesday, as part of the fourth round of the league phase. This comes amid uncertainty regarding the participation of the Emirati team, given the developments unfolding in the region and the disruptions to air travel.
 These developments follow the refusal of the Emirati club Al-Wasl to travel to Saudi Arabia to face Al-Nassr in the same tournament last week. This decision was prompted by regional conditions and disruptions to air travel, which led the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to postpone the match to a later date.
 Potential penalties in the event of withdrawal
 According to the Okaz newspaper, the tournament regulations treat a withdrawal without a valid excuse as a withdrawal from the entire competition. Therefore, it is not considered a withdrawal from just one match, and all results of the withdrawing team may be nullified.
 Potential penalties include a fine of at least $50,000 if the withdrawal occurs during the league stage. The club could also be banned from participating in one or more AFC competitions.
 Shandong Taishan precedent
 The report was based on the punishment imposed by the AFC on the Chinese club Shandong Taishan. This was after his withdrawal from the match against Ulsan Hyundai, South Korea, on February 19, 2025.
 The Disciplinary and Ethics Committee then decided to ban the Chinese club from participating in continental competitions until the 2026-2027 season. In addition, it was fined $50,000.
 The penalties also included requiring Shandong Taishan to refund its $600,000 participation fee and $200,000 performance bonus, as well as paying $40,000 in damages to Ulsan Hyundai.
 The possibility of imposing sanctions on Al-Ahli remains contingent on the circumstances of the match and the club’s stance. Any decisions made by the Asian Football Confederation will also depend on the applicable regulations.
